chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Ibn Fazzal from Mansur ibn Yunus from Abu Hamza from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said:

The believer is silent to be safe, and speaks to benefit. He neither discusses his entrustments with the friends nor does he conceal his testimony from the remote ones, nor does he do anything of the goodness for showing off, nor does he neglect it due to bashfulness. If he is praised, he fears what they might be saying, and he seeks Forgiveness of Allah for what they do not know. The words of the ignorant one do not deceive him, and he fears the counting of what he has done.
ai.seo_question: What are the key ethical characteristics and behaviors of a true believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) defines the believer's character through the discipline of speech, distinguishing between protective silence and purposeful speech. It further elaborates on the psychological state of the faithful, who remain humble before public opinion yet vigilant against divine accountability, ensuring their deeds are sincere rather than driven by vanity or modesty.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Mansour Bin Yunus, from Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said:

‘The Momin is silent to be safe, and speaks to benefit. He neither discusses his entrustments of the friends nor does he conceal his testimony from the remote ones, nor does he do anything from the goodness for showing off, nor does he neglect the bashfulness. If he pays Zakāt he fears from what (the people) might be saying, and he seeks Forgiveness of Allahazwj for the ones who are not knowing. The words of the ignorant one do not tempt him, and he fears the ‘counting’ of what he does’.
en.sarwar: 3. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from ibn Faddal from Mansur ibn Yunus from abu Hamza from Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) who has said the following: “

The believer remains silent for safety and speaks to benefit. He does not speak of his trust to the friends and does not withhold his testimony for the people of distant relationships. He does not do anything good to show off and does not ignore it due to bashfulness. If he cleanses himself he fears what they (people) say, and asks forgiveness for what they do not know. The words (in his praise) of those who do not know do not make him boastful and he is afraid of the sum of his deeds.”
